children: Solar Industries says the acquisition is aimed at creating a global platform for commercial explosives and blasting solutions

Solar Industries India is set to acquire South Africa-based chemicals and explosives company Omnia Holdings for around Rs 12,951 crore (USD 1.355 billion) in an all-cash transaction, marking a major overseas expansion for the Nagpur-based company.

The acquisition will be carried out through Solar Industries’ wholly owned step-down subsidiary, Solar SA Investments Proprietary, which has entered into a definitive agreement with Omnia Holdings. The transaction covers all outstanding shares of Omnia and is expected to be completed in early to mid-2027, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

Solar Industries said the acquisition is aimed at creating a global platform for commercial explosives and blasting solutions. The deal will expand the group’s international footprint while adding geographical reach and technological capabilities to its operations.

Omnia has a significant presence in mining and explosives through its businesses across several international markets. Its FY26 consolidated financial statements show operations spanning South Africa, Namibia, Ghana, Canada, the US and other markets.
Following completion, Omnia is expected to be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X Markets.

The acquisition comes as Solar Industries continues to report strong growth in its domestic operations. The company’s net profit rose 92.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 652.6 crore in the quarter ended June 30, while revenue increased 71.2 per cent to Rs 3,688.2 crore.

The deal represents a significant step-up in Solar Industries’ international ambitions, with the company seeking to broaden its presence in the commercial explosives and mining solutions market through the acquisition.
